They will then get one or two responses from these guys, and on the basis of that, they will then form an opinion of which one to choose. What we are looking at doing firstly, this is a very time-consuming process where there are multiple emails which are being exchanged between people, multiple phone calls being exchanged between the customer and either the intermediary or the ocean liner. This will typically, you know, result in, you know, one query will have anywhere upwards of 15 to 20 emails being exchanged because there are so many variables in this.
What we are looking at doing is putting together a technology platform where on a single screen, once you've entered all your input criteria, on a single screen you'll be able to see all the options of various ocean liners and on another screen all the airliners which are available to the customer. This instantly brings more transparency into the market. Today, when we speak to the CFOs or the purchasing heads of some of the large customers that we work with, their constant gripe is that they don't have transparency on what options exist for them. They don't know if their guys have reached out to, you know, if there are five ocean liners who are operating on that route or there is only one operating, right?
They don't know whether the guys have reached out to all five or they've just been lazy and reached out to only one or two. There is no way for them to know whether they've got the best deal available. By having this platform in front of them, it will bring instant transparency to the booking process. That's what we are trying to solve for and move the power literally from the, you know, from the intermediary. As a platform, bring the power to the hands of the consumer.
Lisa Thompson
Senior Technology Analyst, Zacks Investment Research
All right. Are you getting paid as a subscription service, or do you get a piece of the transaction?
Dhruv Shringi
CEO and Co-Founder, Yatra Online
At this point in time, it's more based on a piece of a transaction. Yes, longer term, we expect this to become more of a subscription service. Today, because we are coming from a relatively low base and we think there's a lot of growth opportunity out here, it's more revenue accretive, we think, to be linked to a transaction value which is being processed through the platform.
Lisa Thompson
Senior Technology Analyst, Zacks Investment Research
All right. Good. Going back to international travel, you said, India's opened up somewhat to that. Has any more countries been opened up since the quarter ended, and which ones are left that are meaningful that you would like to see open?
Dhruv Shringi
CEO and Co-Founder, Yatra Online
See, today we are at a stage where pretty much everything is open. There are very limited restrictions. There still are some restrictions around, you know, people needing to have booster shots in place when they're traveling to certain countries in Europe or needing, you know, RT-PCR tests to be done. Otherwise, you know, most countries are today open. That way we are seeing very strong recovery happening in international travel. One of the reasons why I said international travel is still at a lower level compared to domestic is because the international airfares are still quite high. International airlines flying from India, especially westbound, have to avoid flying over Ukrainian airspace or Russian airspace. That extends the flying time and hence the price of the ticket.
The lag which is there in consumer spend typically that we would have seen on international travel is being made up today by business travelers. Out of India, it's today virtually impossible to get a seat to Europe or the US in front of the aircraft. Business class, first class, the recovery over there has happened at a much faster pace than economy travel out of India to Europe and US. That's been driven largely by recovery in the business travel side of things.
Lisa Thompson
Senior Technology Analyst, Zacks Investment Research
All right. Great. Thank you. That's all my questions.
Dhruv Shringi
CEO and Co-Founder, Yatra Online
Sure. Thank you.

Thank you. There's a follow-up question from Anja Soderstrom in Sidoti.

Senior Equity Research Analyst, Sidoti
Yes. Hi. Thank you for taking my follow-up question. I'm just curious, with the shortage of pilots and the crews that we see here in the US and bottlenecks at the airports in Europe specifically, how do you think that might affect your business in the coming quarters and months? And how is that also, how is India faring with this, those same kind of problems?

I think there are two aspects to it. What we are seeing, firstly, is that Indian carriers are able to ramp up faster because they don't face the same crew constraints. Some of the European carriers are definitely facing this as a challenge. The supply on certain European routes is still lesser than where it was pre-COVID levels. What we are also seeing is some of the Middle Eastern carriers step in aggressively to try and muscle into those routes. While the European carriers might be losing a bit of market share, we think some of the Middle Eastern carriers are gaining at their expense. Overall, from a passenger perspective, we are seeing enough supply being available. It's just that it might not be the most direct route which was available earlier.
Some of the flights on the direct routes might be limited, but at least the option to fly via some of the Middle Eastern cities is definitely available to customers.
Anja Soderstrom
Senior Equity Research Analyst, Sidoti
Okay, thank you. That was helpful.

Yep.
